symptom: v0.3–v0.6 regressions need benchmarks/checkouts/*, which is gitignored and was never recreated by any script; a clean checkout silently reports 0 tasks as N/A / recall 0
rootCause: pinned repositories were cloned by hand during development (hidden state)
fix: benchmarks/fetch-checkouts.ts (npm run benchmark:checkouts) fetches each pinned commit (sparse for keycloak); benchmark:v03 runs it first

step: [v0.9] README tarball validation in a fresh clone
symptom: `npm pack` fails in a fresh clone because prepack runs tsc before dependencies are installed; README also named context-slice-0.8.0.tgz and said 'Only Java source is supported in v0.7' / 'After linking ContextSlice'
rootCause: README written from an already-installed development checkout
fix: README adds `npm ci` before `npm pack`, names the current tarball, and drops stale version wording
regressionTest: tests/package-metadata.test.ts (README tarball name matches package version)

step: [v0.9] git status in target repository after init
symptom: `?? .context-slice/` appears in the developer's git status
rootCause: cache directory was not ignored and ContextSlice (correctly) does not edit the repository .gitignore
fix: cache directory writes its own `.gitignore` containing `*`; also applied to caches created by 0.8.0 on first use after upgrade

symptom: v0.8 report printed 'Path with spaces: false' and 'Nested cwd: false' while claiming status pass
rootCause: macOS tmpdir is a symlink (/var -> /private/var); the check compared the symlinked path with the real path the CLI reports
fix: smoke test uses realpathSync for its workspace

symptom: no documented way to remove repository caches; uninstall leaves them
rootCause: undocumented behavior
fix: README documents `rm -rf .context-slice`; no `clean` command added (one rm is simpler than a new CLI surface)
regressionTest: clean-room RC run (uninstall step verifies cache retention)

symptom: `status` on a never-initialized repository creates an empty .context-slice/ cache while reporting UNINITIALIZED
rootCause: IndexStorage opens (and creates) the SQLite cache on every command
fix: accepted: the directory is self-ignored and contains no source; documented that ContextSlice only writes to .context-slice/

symptom: a non-SQLite index.sqlite produced `INTERNAL_ERROR: file is not a database` (exit 1) and advised `context-slice doctor`, which fails the same way
rootCause: SQLite open errors were not mapped to the existing INDEX_CORRUPT workflow error
fix: IndexStorage raises INDEX_CORRUPT (exit 2) with remediation `rm -rf .context-slice && context-slice init`
regressionTest: tests/cache.test.ts (corrupt cache fails with an actionable INDEX_CORRUPT error)

step: [v0.9] Codex integration (codex exec with command context-slice, args [mcp])
symptom: codex-cli 0.153.4 ended the turn with 'You've hit your usage limit' before any MCP tool call
rootCause: assistant account quota on this host, not ContextSlice
fix: none needed in ContextSlice; the RC script now reports a pre-tool runtime failure as DEFERRED instead of FAIL. Rerun `npm run release:rc -- --assistants` once quota resets

step: [v0.9] preview on spring-petclinic: "explain the owner update flow"
symptom: target resolves to OwnerController.initUpdateOwnerForm (the GET form handler) with 1 item / 32 tokens, and no callers or callees; processUpdateOwnerForm is the more useful target
rootCause: task-text target ranking prefers the first matching handler; ranking changes are feature work outside v0.9 scope
fix: accepted for v0.9; name the symbol in the task (e.g. "explain processUpdateOwnerForm") for a richer slice

symptom: package version moved 0.9.0 -> 1.0.0; README, CHANGELOG, release notes and tests reference the new tarball name
rootCause: planned release step, not a defect
fix: package.json is the single source of truth; tests/package-metadata.test.ts asserts the version and that README names context-slice-<version>.tgz

symptom: codex exec connected and called context.preview, but Codex refused it: 'MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never'
rootCause: validation harness ran codex exec without an approval mode; non-interactive runs need --approve-for-me. Not a ContextSlice defect: the server connected, the tool was visible and the arguments were correct
fix: clean-room script passes --approve-for-me; rerun succeeded and returned the expected target symbol

symptom: upgrade and downgrade steps reported FAIL although the recorded behavior was correct
rootCause: the assertions hard-coded the previous version as 0.8.0 while the v1.0 baseline is 0.9.0
fix: assertions read the baseline version from the baseline checkout's package.json

symptom: every source file of 32KB or more was silently skipped, including Excalidraw's 454KB App.tsx
rootCause: the tree-sitter node binding rejects a string input of 32KB or more; the parse threw and was recorded only as a parse error
fix: parse through a chunked input callback (4KB slices)
regressionTest: benchmark parse-error counts (nest-core 0, excalidraw 4 of 597) plus tests/typescript.test.ts parse-error case

symptom: UNIQUE constraint failure on symbols.id when two declarations shared a canonical identity
rootCause: the TypeScript parser did not disambiguate duplicate identities the way the Java parser does
fix: append #n to duplicate identities and repoint their call edges

symptom: top-level statements produced no call edges, so a small app showed almost no calls
rootCause: calls were only attributed to enclosing callables, and much TypeScript code lives at module scope
fix: a synthetic module symbol named after the file owns top-level statements and their calls

step: [v1.1] v1.1 build after fetching TypeScript benchmark checkouts
symptom: npm run build compiled the checked-out third-party TypeScript repositories and failed
rootCause: tsconfig included benchmarks/**/*.ts and the new checkouts are TypeScript
fix: tsconfig excludes benchmarks/checkouts and tests/fixtures
regressionTest: npm test (package smoke runs npm pack, which builds)

symptom: a synthetic module symbol named after the file's basename collided with an exported symbol of the same name, making preview targets ambiguous
rootCause: module symbols were named after the basename
fix: module symbols are named by file path, which cannot shadow a declared symbol

symptom: missing required facts were attributed to missing type resolution when they were really neighbouring declarations the slice did not include
rootCause: coarse attribution heuristic in the benchmark script
fix: TYPE_RESOLUTION is claimed only when the fact sits behind a call the resolver could not follow; otherwise CONTEXT_COMPOSITION
regressionTest: benchmark report records the attribution per fact

symptom: two required facts about sibling class members are not in the slice for a method target
rootCause: a preview for a method includes callers and callees, not the rest of the enclosing class
fix: accepted and reported: required-fact recall is 95.56%, not 100%, and the gap is attributed to context composition rather than hidden

symptom: the 1.0.0 CLI cannot use a cache written by 1.1.0: it exits 1 with a SQLite error until `.context-slice` is deleted
rootCause: the 1.1.0 schema adds a NOT NULL language column, and the already-released 1.0.0 code inserts without it. 1.0.0 cannot be changed retroactively
fix: documented in the changelog, release notes and docs/typescript-support.md: downgrading requires `rm -rf .context-slice`. No data is misread; the failure is loud. Forward upgrades and same-shape schema changes rebuild automatically
regressionTest: clean-room downgrade step asserts the failure is loud and that cleanup restores it

symptom: `init` reported "Indexed 10 Java files" in a TypeScript repository, and `doctor` labelled its check "java-source"
rootCause: wording predating multi-language support
fix: init reports source files with a per-language breakdown; the doctor check is named "source"
regressionTest: tests/cli.test.ts and tests/typescript.test.ts assert the wording

symptom: nested callables had no enclosing symbol, so component closures had no siblings to compose
rootCause: the TypeScript parser set parentId only for class members
fix: nested callables record their enclosing callable; a bare call now resolves to the nearest lexical scope instead of module level only

symptom: Java siblings sharing a field were not detected
rootCause: Java fields are not indexed as symbols
fix: field declarations are read from the enclosing type's source for analysis only; nothing is added to the index, so Java retrieval and ranking are unchanged
regressionTest: tests/composition.test.ts (Java field sharing without indexing fields)

symptom: composition cost Java slices 1.19 points of median context reduction while recovering no fact there
rootCause: the enclosing-type skeleton was added regardless of how much budget the primary context had used
fix: composition may use at most 35% of the budget; Java cost fell to 0.63 points and skeleton efficiency rose from 3.29 to 11.56 facts per 1k tokens

symptom: four of five composition rules recovered no required fact across the 30 benchmark tasks while costing 966 tokens, and Java lost 0.63 points of context reduction
rootCause: the rules were kept on a targeted fixture corpus written to justify them, not on measured benefit
fix: removed shared-state, accessor, constructor-dependency and lexical-closure composition with their fixtures and tests; only the enclosing-type skeleton remains. Java context reduction returned to 94.55% and TypeScript recall stayed at 100%
regressionTest: tests/composition.test.ts (4 tests) and the v1.2 benchmark comparison

symptom: tree-sitter-python 0.23 could not be installed: it requires tree-sitter >=0.22 while Java and TypeScript grammars pin 0.21.1
rootCause: peer dependency conflict across grammar packages
fix: pinned tree-sitter-python 0.21.0, which matches the existing core; no grammar engine upgrade and no other language touched
regressionTest: npm ci and the package smoke test in the clean-room run

symptom: 17% of relative imports did not resolve, e.g. `from .sansio.app import App`
rootCause: module paths required __init__.py at every level, but Flask's sansio/ is a namespace-style directory without one
fix: module paths anchor at the highest package ancestor, so directories below it without __init__.py still count
regressionTest: v1.3 benchmark reports 100% relative import resolution for all three repositories

symptom: a @t.overload stub shadowed the implementation, so a lookup by name returned three symbols and picked a body-less stub
rootCause: overload signatures were indexed but not marked, and resolveSymbol had no preference
fix: Python overloads are marked like TypeScript ones, and resolveSymbol prefers implementations over overload signatures in both languages
regressionTest: benchmark target resolution for all 15 Python tasks

symptom: the instance-receiver rule appeared to recover no edge
rootCause: the fixture constructed a service but never called a method on it, so the rule was never exercised
fix: fixture calls a method on the constructed instance; each of the three receiver rules now demonstrably recovers an edge no other rule does
